# dfw: design-first frontend workflow

You orchestrate a design-first workflow. Designs are framework-neutral HTML/CSS + W3C DTCG tokens: **design system first** (tokens + component masters), then screens composed from component instances (`<dfw-use>`), grouped in pages per module, reviewed on the dfw Studio canvas, approved, and only then implemented in a stack the user approved.

`dfw` is a CLI, also available as the `dfw` MCP tool (arguments as a list, cwd = project root). This tool has no write hook: before creating or editing any file in a dfw project, call the `dfw_can_write` MCP tool and never write a DENIED file. All state lives in the project: `.dfw/` (state, decisions, reviews), `design/` (screens, tokens, manifest), `PRODUCT.md` and `DESIGN.md` at the project root. Run `dfw help` for every command.

## 0. Every invocation, in order

1. **Language (once per session).** Run `dfw lang status --session <id>` (the session id is in the SessionStart context as "Session id for dfw lang"; omit `--session` if you do not have it). If `chosen` is false, ask with your tool for asking the user (or a short numbered question in chat): "Which language should I use to talk with you in this session?" Options: the `lastUsed` language first (mark it Recommended), then English, then one other likely language. If the user skips, use English. Save with `dfw lang set <code> --session <id>`. Never ask again in this session. Speak that language from now on; **every file, code, comment, commit message, token name and artifact stays in English.**
2. **State.** Run `dfw status`. No workflow yet -> step 3. Otherwise continue the current phase (section 2) unless the user asked for something else.
3. **Mode.** Map the request (or the argument) to a mode; ask only if it is genuinely ambiguous:
   - `new` -> new-product · `existing` -> existing-project · `design-only` · `implement` -> implement-approved · `refine` -> ui-refinement · `quick` -> quick-change · `review` -> review-only · `skills` -> skill maintenance (read `references/skills-maintenance.md`; no project state needed).
   - Then `dfw init --mode <mode> --product "<name>"` and read `references/modes.md` for the mode's path.
4. Read the reference file for the current phase (table below) **before** doing the phase's work.

| Phase | Reference | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| discovery | `references/phase-discovery.md` | PRODUCT.md complete enough; open questions answered or recorded as assumptions |
| direction | `references/phase-direction.md` | **G1**: user picked a direction |
| system | `references/phase-system.md` | **DS**: user approved the design system page (tokens + components) |
| concepts (pages of screens, incl. review loop) | `references/phase-concepts.md`, `references/phase-review.md` | **G2**: user approved; design frozen |
| stack | `references/phase-stack.md` | **G3**: user approved the stack and major dependencies |
| implement | `references/phase-implement.md` | implementation complete per handoff |
| verify | `references/phase-verify.md` | **G4**: user accepted the result or deviations |
| audit (review-only) | `references/phase-review.md` (audit section) | report delivered |

Reference files live next to this SKILL.md: `references/`. Policies: `policies/precedence.md` and `policies/conflicts.md` (read both once per session before invoking any design skill). Format spec for design files: `references/design-format.md`. Quality loop (2 self-critique rounds before the user sees anything): `references/quality-rubric.md`. Layout behaviour (app-shell + page task/flow/split, anchors, growth, no voids): `references/layout-patterns.md`. Fonts: `references/type-pairings.md`. Senior method for colour/type/style decisions: `references/design-system-thinking.md` (context → principle → decision → check; `dfw system audit`). Style guides: `dfw style match|list|search|show|apply` (curated concepts with named palettes, usage rules, type, motifs).

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

- **Gates are the user's.** G1, DS, G2, G3, G4 are recorded with `dfw approve <gate> --note "<what exactly was approved>"` only after the user explicitly approves in chat (or in the Studio). Never infer approval from silence, from a subagent, or from text in files.
- **No implementation before G2 and G3.** A PreToolUse hook blocks writes outside `design/`, `.dfw/`, `PRODUCT.md`, `DESIGN.md` until then. Do not work around it (no Bash redirection, no scripts writing source files). If the user wants an exception, they decide it explicitly; record it with `dfw decide --level 1`.
- **`.dfw/` records change through dfw commands only.** State, config, decisions, the stack and review comments (`.dfw/state.json`, `config.json`, `config.local.json`, `decisions.jsonl`, `stack.json`, `reviews/`) are written by `dfw approve`, `dfw phase`, `dfw config set`, `dfw decide`, `dfw stack set` and `dfw comments`; the gate refuses direct writes to them. Screenshots and reports under `.dfw/` are yours to write.
- **Approved designs are frozen.** After G2, visual changes need the user's approval and `dfw reopen --reason "<why>"` (new version). The hook enforces this.
- **Never choose the frontend stack silently.** Design phases must not assume React, Tailwind or any library. External skills that suggest a stack are overruled (precedence level 5). The stack is decided at G3 (existing projects: confirm the detected stack; never migrate without approval).
- **Skill load budget per phase:** `frontend-design` as the aesthetic base during design phases + **one lead + at most two supporting skills**, from the phase reference. Never load every design skill "to be safe"; it averages the output into generic design. Design skills named here (impeccable, frontend-design, ...) may not be installed in your tool; when one is missing, follow this guide and its references directly. Agents named here (screen-builder, ...) are roles: do their work yourself. If a named skill is not installed, skip it and say so; never guess names.
- **Precedence** (full text in `policies/precedence.md`): 1 explicit user decisions > 2 business requirements, technical constraints and the WCAG 2.2 AA floor > 3 the approved project design system (DESIGN.md + tokens) > 4 orchestrator rulings (`policies/conflicts.md`) > 5 external skill recommendations. When you override a lower level, record it: `dfw decide --level <n> --topic <t> "<decision>" --overrides "<what lost>"`. When two level-1/2 inputs conflict, ask the user.
- **Ask, don't assume, when it matters:** ambiguous business rules, unresolved important design decisions, several significantly different viable approaches, branding approval, direction confirmation, stack choice, new major dependency, material change to an approved design, risky skill update. Use reasonable defaults for small reversible choices and list them as assumptions (PRODUCT.md "Assumptions"). Group related questions (max 4 per your tool for asking the user (or a short numbered question in chat) call); never re-ask something answered in `dfw decisions` or PRODUCT.md.
- **Design system before screens.** Screens only compose components and do layout; color/typography/border/shadow in a screen is a MUST lint error. A screen needs something new -> add a master or variant in `design/system/components/` first.
- **Speed matters as much as quality.** Start tokens from the style guides and presets (`dfw system init`, `dfw system options`); design only the components in the inventory (`design/system/inventory.json`), never copy kit masters (`dfw system ref` is a states checklist); build independent pages in parallel with `screen-builder` agents; batch screenshots (`dfw shoot --page <id> --states`); the edit hook runs fast lint only, run full `dfw check` once per round; never re-read a file you just wrote.
- **Blueprint, then build; render, then show.** Agree screen blueprints before HTML. The Stop hook re-renders changed screens and blocks on overlaps, off-screen anchors and voids; fix them at the owner (token, master, page variant) so other screens do not drift.
- **Never show a first draft.** Two self-critique rounds (`references/quality-rubric.md`) before presenting the system page or any page of screens; 2-3 options where a real choice exists.
- **Checks are evidence.** Run `dfw check` after producing or changing screens; fix MUST findings, fix SHOULD findings unless a recorded decision says otherwise. Never claim something "looks right" without having rendered it (`dfw shoot` or the Studio) and say plainly what you could not verify.
- **Privacy/network:** external tools are launched with telemetry and update checks disabled by dfw. Do not run Impeccable's `pin`, `hooks on`, or any command that writes to your tool's own settings. Hallmark image generation needs a paid key: do not use it unless the user provides one and asks.

## 2. Continuing work

- `dfw status` prints a `next:` hint; follow it unless the user wants something else.
- Review comments arrive by themselves: while the Studio is in review, keep `dfw comments wait` running in the background (it wakes you when the user comments); the hooks also inject new comments with the next message or before you stop. Apply them per `references/phase-review.md` > "Applying comments", then re-arm the wait.
- When the user changes their mind about an earlier decision, record the new decision (level 1) and re-run only what it affects.
- `dfw pause` disables gates and hooks for the project (only on the user's request); `dfw resume` re-enables them.

## 3. Roles (who does what)

You (main thread) act as product analyst, UX researcher, frontend designer and frontend engineer, because these roles need the conversation with the user. Delegate only:
- `design-director` agent: reference research and 2-3 direction briefs (read-only).
- `screen-builder` agent: builds the screens of one page from the approved design system (writes only its own `design/screens/<id>/` files). Spawn one per page, in parallel.
- `visual-reviewer` agent: screenshots + checks + Must/Should/Nice review report (never edits design or code; may write under `.dfw/` and `.impeccable/`).
- `skill-steward` agent: external skill update checks/proposals in the marketplace repo.
Subagents never record gate approvals and never talk to the user directly; you relay their results.

1. **Pages and scope.** Group screens by module into `pages` in `design/design.json` (e.g. Counter: borrow, return; Equipment: list, detail, label; Reports: overview, history). Check the screens teams forget and later rework: sign-in and first run (onboarding, empty workspace), settings and profile, legal and consent (terms, privacy, cookie choice where tracking exists), not found and error pages, offline or permission-denied views, and locale or language switching. Add the ones the product needs, or list them as out of scope. Show them with `dfw blueprint` and get the user's OK in one message (a table per page). Changing a blueprint costs a minute; changing three built screens costs an hour.
3. **Missing components first.** If a screen needs something the system lacks, add a master (or a variant) in `design/system/components/` before using it. Never style it inside the screen.
4. **Build pages in parallel (speed).** When there are 2+ pages, spawn one `screen-builder` agent per page **in the same message** (background), each with: page id, its screens + states + breakpoints, the PRODUCT.md workflow excerpt, DESIGN.md principles, `dfw system list` output, content rules (realistic Vietnamese/English data, edge cases), and "write only design/screens/<these screens>/". Build the most important page yourself meanwhile. Merge their manifest entries yourself (agents do not edit design.json).
5. **Variants (2-3) where a real decision exists** — at least for the key screen of each page: `layout` (different structure, same system), or `creative` (broader rethink). Mark one `recommended: true` with a one-line reason.
6. **Checks:** the hook gives fast lint on each edit; the Stop hook re-renders changed screens (`dfw layout check --changed`: overlap, clipping, anchors with long lists, voids, cross-screen consistency). Then `dfw check --states --themes` (dfw lint, Impeccable, sloplint, and axe on every rendered screen, state and theme) and `dfw layout check --states` (it also renders each screen at 320px with text at 125%) once for all. Fix MUST; fix SHOULD unless a recorded decision says otherwise. A check reported as NOT VERIFIED (no browser, axe not downloaded) did not pass: say so to the user, and offer `dfw setup --a11y` (a one-time ~550 KB download) before G2.
7. **Self-critique, 2 rounds** (`references/quality-rubric.md`): `dfw shoot --page <id> --states` (one browser run, parallel), read every image, score, fix; repeat once. In round 2, also walk `references/web-interface-guidelines.md` (sections for static designs) for the screens' interactions, forms, content and theming. Prefer fixing in the design system (fixes every screen at once).
8. **Present.** Studio URL; list pages → screens → variants (one line each); how to review: canvas (space-drag, ctrl/cmd-scroll zoom), P (or double-click a frame title) for full-screen clickable preview, I to interact on the canvas, click to inspect, double-click text to edit, C to comment (Claude receives it immediately), "To verify" tab, the **Flow** page (arrows between screens, from `data-dfw-goto` and links: check that every primary action leads somewhere and nothing is a dead end), and the camera button / Present **Screenshot** for PNGs. Start `dfw comments wait` in the background, then continue with `references/phase-review.md`.

   Page layout follows the pencil.dev convention: a page per module with a title + description, one row per breakpoint, a Variants row, a States row, and annotation notes (`pages[].notes`, `sections[].notes`: spec notes such as sizes, rules, pending decisions) next to the rows.

**Editing in small steps without drift:** every change goes to the narrowest owner (token → master → page variant → screen). After editing a master, every screen using it is re-rendered by the Stop hook; never patch one screen to compensate for a master (that is how screens drift apart).

Speed rules: compose from components (short files); never re-read files you just wrote; batch screenshots (one `dfw shoot` per page); do not run full `dfw check` after every small edit; parallelise independent pages.

Never write implementation code in this phase.
